key_features.classic_presentation: Peptic ulcer disease presents with EPIGASTRIC PAIN that is BURNING or GNAWING in quality, 5-8/10 severity. Pain has a CHARACTERISTIC TIMING PATTERN: DUODENAL ulcers improve with food and worsen 2-5 hours after meals (empty stomach), while GASTRIC ulcers worsen with food. Pain is often NOCTURNAL (wakes patient at night). Onset is chronic/recurrent over weeks to months. Key associated symptoms: Nausea, bloating, early satiety. Location: Epigastric, midline. Key history: NSAID use, H. pylori infection history, smoking, alcohol. Key positives: Pain relieved by antacids, predictable pattern with meals, nocturnal pain. Key negatives: NEW ONSET severe pain may indicate perforation. Vomiting blood (hematemesis) or black tarry stools (melena) indicates bleeding ulcer requiring urgent evaluation. Weight loss suggests gastric cancer, not simple ulcer.

red_flags: Sudden severe epigastric pain with peritoneal signs - perforated ulcer, call 911
Vomiting blood or coffee-ground emesis - bleeding ulcer, needs urgent endoscopy
Weight loss with early satiety - gastric cancer, needs urgent endoscopy
